children: ) today announced a five-year extension of its strategic oncology collaboration with AstraZeneca, effective January 1, 2027, through December 31, 2031.

Under the renewed agreement, Tempus and AstraZeneca will extend their collaboration, leveraging de-identified multimodal data, integrated scientific intelligence, clinical trial network access and strategic initiatives to accelerate drug discovery and clinical development.

"Five years ago, Tempus and AstraZeneca entered into a landmark collaboration—our first enterprise-wide data deal across a global pharmaceutical company's entire oncology portfolio," said Eric Lefkofsky, founder and CEO of Tempus. "Since then, our teams have made significant progress integrating data and AI into drug discovery and development. We're honored to extend this partnership for another five years and accelerate our work on behalf of patients worldwide."

Under the terms of the extension, AstraZeneca will receive expanded access to Lens, Tempus’ data analytics platform, as well as advanced compute capabilities and a library of de-identified patient records with matched clinical and molecular data. Additionally, the renewal supports continued collaboration across Tempus’ broader suite of offerings, including clinical trial matching, Next-generation sequencing (NGS) laboratory testing, biomarker studies and model development.

“AI continues to play an increasingly important role in how we develop medicines by allowing us to draw deeper biological and molecular insights from data,” said Susan Galbraith, Executive Vice President, Oncology Haematology R&D, AstraZeneca. “These insights help us identify and select the patients most likely to benefit from an investigative therapy, increasing the probability of success in the clinic.”
This strategic collaboration is in addition to Tempus’ foundation model work with AstraZeneca and Pathos.

Tempus is making precision medicine a reality by unlocking a more complete view of patients, supporting better clinical decision making, accelerating better medicines and improving care through the power of connected AI, diagnostics and workflows. With one of the world’s largest libraries of de-identified multimodal data, Tempus has created an intelligent ecosystem that continuously turns data into actionable insights, helping ensure that every patient benefits from the treatment of those who came before.
For more information, visit tempus.com and follow Tempus on LinkedIn, Instagram, and X.
